newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel says Jerusalem bombers from abroad -- Arafat.
newsitem.headline: Israel says Jerusalem bombers from abroad -- Arafat.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat said on Friday Israel had informed him the bombers who killed 13 people and themselves in a Jerusalem market last month came from abroad.
"They informed us, the Israeli security officers, that they (bombers) came from abroad," Arafat told Israel Television.
Arafat was asked why, in that case, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu blamed him for the bombing.
"This is what I want to ask you," Arafat replied. "I want to ask the Israeli people. Unless the objective is to scrap the partnership between us and the goal is to destroy the peace process."
The identity of the attackers who set off the bombs that ripped through the market on July 30 is still unknown. More than 170 people were injured in the attack.
Israel reacted by suspending peace talks with the Palestinian Authority and demanded Arafat crack down on Islamic militants, insisting he had not done enough to fight "terrorism".
The Moslem militant Hamas and Islamic Jihad groups have killed scores of Israelis in suicide bombings since 1994.
"You have to know that this attack was not carried out by either Hamas or Islamic Jihad. It is clear they came from abroad without cooperation from here," Arafat said.
Netanyahu has said even if the bombers did come from abroad, they must have been helped by Arab militants operating in Palestinian-ruled areas.
In the aftermath of the bombing Israel sealed off the West Bank and the Gaza Strip -- stopping trade, preventing Palestinians from reaching jobs in Israel and freezing financial transfers.
Arafat has slammed the blockade as a declaration of war and told Palestinians to "prepare for what will come".
Asked about these comments, Arafat said he was "trying to calm the people".
"I said what I said to encourage the people to tolerate this suffering and then you come and accuse me. What do you want me to tell the people? Go onto the streets?

"I want to ask Netanyahu a question, Netanyahu who considers himself a politician. A whole nation of 3 million people -- doesn't he think that this is going to have an effect on them? Aren't all these policies encouragement to the extremist forces?"
